To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the product of ORF P is a repressor of its cognate gene, that ORF P binds to p32 in cells infected with herpes simplex virus, that the ORF P product represses the expression of key regulatory genes in cells infected with recombinant viruses, and that the ORF O protein inhibits the binding of ICP4 to its cognated site.
ORF O protein binds to and inhibiting ICP4, the major regulatory protein of herpes simplex virus, thereby blocking the synthesis of key regulatory proteins essential for productive infection.

the expression of ORFs P and O is repressed in productive infection, ORF O initiators translation from a methionine codone of ORF P, and the product of ORF 0 binds and inhibits in in vitro binding of ICP4 to its cognates site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the expression of the ORFs P and O in the context of the viral genome.
the mechanisms by which the synthesis of viral regulatory proteins is repressed during latent infection.
the regulation of the expression of ORFs P and O and their products, which are transcribed from the same DNA strand and are located within the domain transcribed in latently infected cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ORF P protein and ORF O protein, together, are capable of inhibiting the synthesis of regulatory proteins required for productive infection.

the ORF O and P genes are transcribed in the latent state of infection and are expressed in a manner that would reduce or eliminate the expression of viral regulatory proteins essential for productive infection.

the expression of the ORFs P and O, which are transcribed in the same direction from opposite strands of the DNA, is repressed in productive infection by ICP4, and the ORF O protein binds to and inhibiting in vitro binding of ICP4 to its cognated site on DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ICP4 is a major repressor of the expression of ORFs P and O and that these ORFs encode proteins which bind to and inhibit ICP4 binding to its cognates site on DNA.
the HSV1 genome contains a mechanism that is able to reduce the expression of regulatory genes during productive infection and increase their expression during latent infection.
ORF P/ORF O proteins may have a role during latent infection in preventing reactivation of the virus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ORF O protein binds to and inhibiting the binding of the major herpes simplex virus regulatory protein, ICP4, to its cognate sequence on DNA.

ORF P, ORF O, and ICP4 are involved in a regulatory loop, in which ICP4 represses the synthesis of ORFP and ORFO, which in turn inhibit the binding of ICP4 to its cognatesite, thereby derepressing the expression of ORFP and ORO.
the ORF O and P genes are expressed in latently infected cells, and the ORF O protein binds and inhibits ICP4, the major viral regulatory factor.
